headline: All majors below the 200-day line with momentum fading; whales moving coins off-exchange while spot ETF demand for Bitcoin dries up.
paragraphs: The regime is intact and weak. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, DOGE, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day moving averages, and none of them have a golden cross to signal a trend reversal pending. The market as a whole is in downtrend: seven majors below the long-term line, zero above it. Bitcoin sits at 63,653, off 49 percent from its 12-month peak of 124,773, while Ethereum is down 60.6 percent from 4,829. The entirety of that severity is visible in the spark range (the 90-day high-low band): Bitcoin has room between 58,550 and 82,145; Ethereum spans 1,564 to 2,368. These bands tell you where the consolidation has been, and they show a market that has been grinding sideways within a significantly lower envelope than it occupied a year ago.

Momentum is mixed and mostly not accelerating the trend lower. Bitcoin's RSI sits at 47.4 (neutral to slightly weak) and its MACD is below signal, confirming the downtrend; Ethereum's RSI is healthier at 56.3, but MACD is still negative and the price is below the 200-day line anyway. Solana's RSI is at 42.7 (oversold-leaning) while MACD is below signal. The one note of interest: BNB and DOGE both have MACD above signal (momentum turning up), but neither has reclaimed the 200-day line and BNB's RSI is flat at 48.3 while DOGE's is very low at 40.7. This is a potential early-stage divergence: momentum trying to roll over while price stays depressed, which is often a false start rather than a sustained reversal. Ethereum is the only asset posting a positive weekly return (1.81 percent over seven days) despite being down 2.97 percent on the month; everyone else is negative to flat over the week.

Derivatives positioning reveals a crowded long-side and mixed pricing. Bitcoin funding is at 0.48 percent annualized (5.2 percent annually), a modest premium that reflects some willingness to hold longs but not expensive. Ethereum funding has flipped negative at negative 0.6 percent annualized, meaning shorts are paying longs to stay in the trade, a sign of short crowding. Both have heavy open interest: Bitcoin at 2.01 billion and Ethereum at 1.32 billion. The long-short ratio on Bitcoin is 1.93 (nearly two longs for every short) and Ethereum's is 2.0, meaning the leverage crowd is tilted long but not insanely so. The real signal is in liquidations: over 24 hours, Bitcoin liquidated 692 positions with longs taking the larger loss (4.49 million to shorts' 3.29 million), and Ethereum saw 1,576 liquidations with longs again hit harder (10.7 million to 7.1 million). Solana's 2.61 long-short ratio is stretched (long-heavy), and DOGE's 4.62 is extremely long-skewed; both saw longs liquidated more than shorts. This positioning is not expensive by absolute standards, but the liquidation pattern shows that the long side is getting flushed on downside moves, typical of a market testing conviction.

Whale and institutional flows tell an important story of divergence. Over the last 48 hours, 351.6 million dollars in Bitcoin moved off-exchange (to cold storage or self-custody), with the three largest moves being 164.9 million from crypto.com and two moves from Kraken (113.5 million and 73 million). This is supply moving away from trading venues, a sign of long-term holding or accumulation by entities that believe spot prices are low. However, the spot ETF picture is the opposite: Bitcoin ETFs posted a 265.4 million dollar net outflow on July 31st (the latest print), and while the five-session net is only negative 61.5 million, the pattern shows same-direction days of just 1, meaning outflows are not persistent. Ethereum ETFs are showing small inflows (9 million on the 31st, 10 million net over five sessions), suggesting some institutional interest in altcoin exposure remains. The stablecoin float stands at 303.8 billion, down 1.59 percent over 30 days, so dry powder is not being marshaled; the weekly whale flows show volatility (the last four weeks: 561 million outflow, 146 million inflow, 445 million outflow, 1.07 billion outflow), confirming chop rather than a one-direction move.

Sentiment is in Fear at 27 (within a 30-day range of 20 to 33), placing the crowd near the lower end of anxiety without capitulation. The disparity between the sentiment gauge and the tape is notable: the fear indicator is not extreme, yet whales are accumulating coins off-exchange while spot buyers are simultaneously leaving ETFs. Total market cap is up 1.19 percent on the day to 2.25 trillion, and Bitcoin dominance is 56.3 percent, stable and high. The smaller movers reveal fragmentation: ENA, ALGO, and M are up 8 to 10 percent, while BEAT is down 26.3 percent, showing that the broad weakness is not uniform and speculation is still active in smaller names.

Watch for a reclaim of the 200-day moving average on any of the majors, starting with Bitcoin and Ethereum as the anchors; that would be the first sign the regime has shifted. Monitor whether the whale accumulation (coins moving to cold storage) accelerates or reverses over the coming week, and whether spot ETF outflows stabilize or persist. The liquidation pattern on the long side bears watching: if downside moves continue to flush longs more aggressively than shorts, conviction is being tested. Finally, the MACD-above-signal on BNB and DOGE are early and not yet confirmed by price or trend, but if those divergences start to resolve into actual price moves above the 200-day line, that would be your signal that the regime itself is beginning to turn.
